props.headline: HACKERS HAVE BREACHED ANTHROPIC'S "TOO DANGEROUS TO RELEASE" MYTHOS AI MODEL
props.tagline: THE LINE BETWEEN SAFETY AND VULNERABILITY JUST GOT THINNER

props.contextText: Here's the report that broke the story:

lines: > "can hack every major OS and browser"
> dario: "we're the safe & responsible ai lab"
The group also has access to other unreleased Anthropic models.
Not just Mythos. The whole pipeline.
Anthropic's statement: "investigating a report of access through one of our third-party vendor environments."
Mythos got breached on day one.

caption:
Anthropic is investigating a case where its restricted "Mythos" model was accessed by a small group of unauthorized users shortly after it was announced.

Mythos is not a public model — it is part of a controlled program used for advanced cybersecurity testing, with capabilities focused on finding software vulnerabilities and generating exploit strategies.

Reports suggest the access did not come from breaking Anthropic's core systems, but through a third-party pathway, likely involving leftover contractor credentials and predictable internal URL structures linked to a vendor environment.

The model was originally limited to select partners under a program called Project Glasswing, meaning exposure came from the surrounding ecosystem rather than the model itself.

Anthropic says it is reviewing the incident and there is no confirmed evidence of malicious use so far, but it highlights how supply chain access points can become weak links when deploying high capability AI systems.
